Rashi on Gittin 63a:10:1.hebrew: לא קבלה - דקתני "זכי לה" ו"התקבל לה", קאי אהולכה — א"אשתך אמרה הבא לי", דאיהי נמי שליח לקבלה שויתיה, שהרי אמרה לו "התקבל". ולקמיה פריך: אם רצה לחזור, אמאי יחזור:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:10:1.english: No, receipt - [The language of receipt,] where [the baraita] teaches "Acquire [it] for her" and "Receive [it] for her," refers to [the case of] delivery — to [the agent's statement,] "Your wife said: 'Bring [it] to me,'" where she herself made him an agent for receipt, for she said to him: "Receive [it for me]." And below, [the Gemara] asks: If he wished to retract, why may he retract:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:10:2.hebrew: והולכה - דקתני "הולך ותן לה", קאי א"אשתך אמרה התקבל":
Rashi on Gittin 63a:10:2.english: And delivery - where [the baraita] teaches [that the husband says], "Take [it] and give [it] to her," [this refers] to [the agent's statement,] "Your wife said, 'Receive [it for me]'":

Rashi on Gittin 63a:11:1.hebrew: מכי מטי גט לידיה - דשליח, תיגרש, דהא תרוייהו שליח לקבלה שוייה, ואמאי "אם רצה לחזור יחזור":
Rashi on Gittin 63a:11:1.english: From [the moment] that the bill of divorce reaches his hand - [that] of the agent, she should be divorced, for both of them appointed him an agent for receipt; and why [does the baraita state], "if he wishes to retract, he may retract"?

Rashi on Gittin 63a:11:2.hebrew: ה"ג שמע מינה דאדיבורא דידיה - דשליח סמיך. כלומר: תיפשוט מדקתני "יחזור", דאדיבורא דידיה סמיך, ואיהו א"ל "אשתך אמרה: הבא לי", והא הימניה; ו"התקבל" דקאמר ליה, "התקבל והולך" קאמר. דהכי נמי אוקימנא לעיל: דאי אתמר דרב נחמן איפכא — "התקבל לי גיטי" ו"אשתך אמרה הבא", והוא אמר "הילך כמה שאמרה", ואמר רב נחמן "משיגיע גט לידה מגורשת" — הוה פשטינן מיניה דאדיבורא דשליח סמיך:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:11:2.english: This is the reading: "Conclude from it that on his statement" - [meaning, on the statement] of the agent he relies. That is to say: resolve [the question] from what [the baraita] teaches, "he shall return [it]," that he relies on his [the agent's] statement, for he [the agent] said to him, "Your wife said, 'Bring [it] to me,'" and [the husband] believed him; and [as for] "Accept [it]" that he said to him, he meant "Accept [it] and deliver [it]." For so too did we establish above: that if [the statement] of Rav Nachman had been stated in reverse — [where the wife said,] "Accept my get for me," and [the agent said,] "Your wife said, 'Bring [it],'" and he [the husband] said, "Here it is for you as she said," and Rav Nachman said, "Once the get reaches her hand, she is divorced" — we would have resolved from it that he relies on the statement of the agent:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:12:1.hebrew: הכי השתא התם קאמר ליה הילך כמה שאמרה - הא דאמרן לעיל, דאי אתמר דרב נחמן איפכא כי הא דהכא — "התקבל לי גיטי" ו"אשתך אמרה הבא לי גיטי", והוא אמר "הילך כמה שאמרה", והוה אמר רב נחמן דכשיגיע גט לידה הוא דהויא מגורשת — הוה פשטינן מיניה דאדיבורא דידיה סמיך, דהא קאמר ליה "הילך כמה שאמרה", וכיון דלא מיגרשה בקבלה דהאי, איכא למיפשט מינה בעיין דהשוכר דאיבעיא לן בכי האי גוונא; דהאי "כמה שאמרה" דקאמר, ה"ק לה: מהימנת לי דהכי קאמרה, ובתורת הולכה יהביה ניהליה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:12:1.english: How can [these cases] be compared? There, he said to him, "Here you are, as she said" - [This refers to] what we said above: that if [the statement] of Rav Nachman had been stated in reverse, like this [case] here — [where the wife said,] "Receive my get for me," and [the agent said,] "Your wife said: 'Bring my get for me,'" and he [the husband] said, "Here you are, as she said," and Rav Nachman had said that [only] when the get reaches her hand is she divorced — we would have resolved from it that he relies on his [the agent's] word, since he said to him, "Here you are, as she said," and since she is not divorced through this [agent's] receipt, one could resolve from it our inquiry in [the chapter] HaSokher, where we inquired about a case like this; for [with] this "as she said" that he says, this is what he is saying to him: "You are believed by me that this is what she said," and he gave it to him in the capacity of delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:12:2.english: Here - where [the husband] says to him, "Acquire [it] and accept [it]":

Rashi on Gittin 63a:12:3.hebrew: מי קאמר ליה הילך כמה שאמרה - דתיפשוט בעיין דהשוכר מינה? הא דקתני הכא "יחזור", משום דכיון דאמר ליה השליח: "שליח להולכה עשאתני אשתך", ואיהו הבעל א"ל: "התקבל", אדם יודע שאין הבעל עושה שליח לקבלה, ו"התקבל והולך" קאמר. אבל אי אמר לו: "הילך כמה שאמרה", אימא לך דאדיבורא דידה סמיך ולא הימניה, ובדעתה תלה, ואם רצה לחזור לא יחזור, דתרוייהו שליח לקבלה שוינהו:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:12:3.english: Does he say to him, "Here you are, as she said" - that you should resolve our dilemma of [the chapter] HaSokher from it? That which it teaches here, "he may retract," is because since [the agent] said to him, "Your wife made me an agent for delivery," and he [the husband] said to him, "Receive [it]," a person knows that [a husband] does not appoint an agent for receipt, and [thus] he meant, "Receive [it] and deliver [it]." However, if he had said to him, "Here you are, as she said," I would say to you that he relied on her statement and did not trust him [the agent], and made it dependent on her intent; and if he wished to retract, he could not retract, for both of them made him an agent for receipt:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:13:1.hebrew: ת"ר כו' רצה לחזור לא יחזור - קסבר: "הולך" כ"זכי" דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:13:1.english: The Sages taught, etc., [if] he seeks to retract, he cannot retract - He [i.e., the first Tanna] holds [that saying] "deliver" is like [saying] "acquire":

Rashi on Gittin 63a:14:1.hebrew: אמר לו אי אפשי שתקבל - גלי דעתיה ד"הולך" דקאמר ליה, לאו "זכי" הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:14:1.english: [If] he said to him, "I do not want you to receive [it]" - he revealed his intention that [the expression] "deliver" that he said to him is not [meant as] "acquire [it on her behalf]":

Rashi on Gittin 63a:16:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: הילך לרבי נתן, כזכי דמי או לא:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:16:1.english: This is the reading [of the text]: [If he said,] "Here you are" — according to Rabbi Natan, is it like "Acquire," or not?

Rashi on Gittin 63a:17:1.hebrew: האשה שאמרה התקבל לי גיטי - כלומר, ואם אמרה לו מתחלה האשה "התקבל", ונתנו ליה הבעל באחת משתי לשונות הללו, רצה לחזור, לא יחזור:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:17:1.english: A woman who said, "Receive my get for me" - That is to say, if the woman said to him initially, "Receive [my get for me]," and the husband [then] gave it to him using one of these two expressions, [if the husband] seeks to retract, he cannot retract:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:1:1.hebrew: הכי השתא בשלמא אי אתמר איפכא התקבל לי גיטי - אמרה ליה היא, והוא אמר לבעל: "אשתך אמרה הבא לי גיטי", ובעל אמר ליה: "הילך כמה שאמרה" — איכא למיפשט בעיין מדרב נחמן; דאי אמר רב נחמן עלה: "משיגיע גט לידו מגורשת", איכא למיפשט דאדיבורא דידה סמיך ולא הימניה, אלא תלה בדעתה ומסריה ניהליה בתורת קבלה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:1:1.english: How now! Granted, if the opposite were stated: "Receive my bill of divorce for me" - [this is what] she said to him, and he said to the husband: "Your wife said: 'Bring me my bill of divorce,'" and the husband said to him: "Here you are, as she said" — [then] we could resolve our question from Rav Nachman; for if Rav Nachman said regarding it: "Once the bill of divorce reaches his hand, she is divorced," we could resolve that he relies upon her statement and did not trust him [the agent], rather he made it dependent on her intention and handed it over to him in the capacity of [an agent of] receipt:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:2:1.hebrew: ואי נמי - הוה אמר רב נחמן עלה "משיגיע גט לידה מגורשת", פשטינן מינה דאדיבורא דידיה סמיך, והימניה דהכי אמרה, ומסריה לידיה בתורת הולכה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:2:1.english: And alternatively - [had] Rav Nachman said regarding it, "Once the get reaches her hand, she is divorced," we would resolve from this that [the husband] relies upon [the agent's] statement, and believed him that she had said so, and handed it over to him as [an agent for] delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:2:2.hebrew: אלא - השתא דאמר רב נחמן "אינה מגורשת", ליכא למיפשט דטעמא משום דסמך אדיבוריה דשליח הוא; דאי נמי אדיבורא דידה סמיך ושויה שליח להולכה, אשמועי' רב נחמן דשליח גופיה לאו בתורת הכי קבליה, דלא ניחא ליה בטירחא דהולכה, ועקריה לשליחותיה ואמר: "שליח לקבלה אפשי להיות, שליח להולכה אי אפשי להיות"; הלכך, אי נמי אמליך ואמטייה ניהלה, לאו גיטא הוא, דמעיקרא לא קבל עליו להיות שליח לבעל להוליך:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:2:2.english: However - Now that Rav Nachman said, "She is not divorced," one cannot resolve [the question by saying] that the reason is because [the husband] relied on the agent's statement; for even if he relied on her statement and appointed him an agent for delivery, Rav Nachman teaches us that the agent himself did not accept [the agency] on those terms, since he does not want the trouble of delivery, and he uprooted his agency and said, "I want to be an agent for receipt; I do not want to be an agent for delivery." Therefore, even if he reconsidered and brought it to her, it is not a [valid] get, because from the outset he did not accept upon himself to be an agent for the husband to deliver [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:3:1.hebrew: ת"ש - תיובתא לרב נחמן:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:3:1.english: Come and hear - [This is] a refutation of Rav Nachman:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:3:2.hebrew: טעמא דרצה לחזור הא לא רצה - ואמטייה לידה, מגורשת:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:3:2.english: The reason is that he wanted to retract; however, [if] he did not want [to retract] - and [the agent] brought it to her hand, she is divorced:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:4:1.english: Why? Isn't the husband ineligible to appoint an agent for receipt - And he gave it [to him] in the capacity of [an agent for] receipt:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:4:2.hebrew: אלא - על כרחיך משום דאמרי', אע"ג דלא יהביה אלא בתורת קבלה, כיון דאמטייה לידה, מיגרשה; משום דכיון שנתן עיניו לגרשה, לכי מתיידע ליה דלא מצי לשוייה שליח לקבלה, ניחא ליה דליהוי שליח להולכה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:4:2.english: Rather - Perforce [it is] because we say [that] even though he only gave it [to him] in the capacity of [an agent for] receipt, once he brings it to her hand, she is divorced; because since he set his eyes on divorcing her, when it becomes known to him that he cannot make him an agent for receipt, it is agreeable to him that he should be an agent for delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:4:3.hebrew: והכא - גבי מילתיה דרב נחמן נמי, אע"ג דההיא שעתא לא נעשה שליח להולכה, מיהו לכי מימליך ואמטייה, מינח ניחא ליה לבעל והוי שלוחו להולכה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:4:3.english: And here - regarding Rav Nachman's statement as well, even though at that moment he was not made an agent for delivery, nevertheless, when he decides and brings it [to her], the husband is pleased with it and he becomes his agent for delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:5:1.hebrew: וגמר ונתן לשם הולכה - והתקבל דקאמר ליה, "התקבל והולך" קאמר; ולא טעמא כדקאמרת הוא, דהיכא דשני ניהוי שליחות:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:5:1.english: And he resolved and gave [it] for the sake of delivery - And [when] he says "Receive" to him, he means "Receive and deliver"; and the reason is not as you said, that wherever he alters [it], it should be [a valid] agency:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:5:2.hebrew: אבל הכא טעי - בעל כסבור שהיא עשאתו שליח לקבלה, דסמך אדיבוריה ולא יהביה ניהליה אלא לשם קבלה. ולרב אשי נמי, דאוקי טעמא דרב נחמן משום דמעיקרא עקריה שליח לשליחותיה, שפיר מיתרצה בהכי — כדתרצינן, דטעמא דמתניתין משום ד"התקבל והולך" קאמר, ומתחילה נעשה שלוחו. ולא איצטריכא למינקט "הכא טעי" אלא אליבא דלישנא קמא, דקא סלקא דעתין טעמא דרב נחמן משום דאדיבורא דידיה סמיך הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:5:2.english: But here he errs - [The] husband thinks that she made him an agent for receipt, for he relied on his [the agent's] word, and he only gave it to him for the sake of receipt. And according to Rav Ashi as well, who established Rav Nachman's reason as being because from the outset the agent uprooted his agency, [the difficulty] is well resolved by this, as we resolved [above], that the reason of the Mishnah is because he said, "Receive and bring," and from the beginning he became his [the husband's] agent. And it was only necessary to state "here he errs" according to the first version, where we had thought that Rav [Nachman]'s reason is because he relied on his [the agent's] word:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:6:1.hebrew: אינו גט עד שיגיע גט לידה - שאין הקטן עושה שליח, הילכך לאו שלוחא דידה הוא, אלא שלוחו דידיה הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:6:1.english: It is not a bill of divorce until the bill of divorce reaches her hand - because a minor cannot appoint an agent; therefore, he is not her agent, rather he is his [the husband's] agent:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:6:2.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: "ואמאי? הא לאו שליח להולכה שוייה":
Rashi on Gittin 63a:6:2.english: This is our reading [of the text]: "But why? [The husband] did not designate him an agent for delivery."

Rashi on Gittin 63a:7:1.hebrew: אדם יודע שאין שליחות לקטן - ואין זה שליח לקבלה, וגמר ונתן לשום הולכה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:7:1.english: A person knows that there is no agency for a minor - and [therefore] this one is not an agent for receipt, and [the husband] resolved and gave [the get] for delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:8:1.english: And "your wife said" - We read [this] in all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:8:2.english: Deliver and give [it] to her, acquire [it] for her, and receive [it] for her - [The husband] said one of all these expressions to him:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:8:3.english: [If] he wishes to retract, he may retract - We explain it as we go along:

Rashi on Gittin 63a:9:1.hebrew: מאי לאו קבלה אקבלה והולכה אהולכה - "זכי והתקבל" דקתני, קאי א"אשתך אמרה התקבל", ו"הולך ותן לה" דקתני, קאי א"אשתך אמרה הבא", וקתני בתרוייהו: משיגיע גט לידה מגורשת. ותיובתא דרב נחמן מקבלה אקבלה, דקתני "הבא לי גיטי" ו"אשתך אמרה התקבל", והוא אומר "התקבל" — דבהדיא יהביה ניהליה בתורת קבלה, ובעל לאו בר הכי הוא, ואיהי נמי לא שויתיה, וקתני דהוי מיהא שליח להולכה, דכיון שנתן עיניו לגרשה כו' כדלעיל; וכ"ש היכא דאמר לו "הילך כמה שאמרה", דאיכא למימר לאו אדיבוריה סמך, אלא בדעתה תלה, ושוייה נמי שליח להולכה:
Rashi on Gittin 63a:9:1.english: What, is it not [a case of] receipt [responding] to receipt, and delivery [responding] to delivery - [The expressions] "acquire [it for her]" and "receive [it for her]" that [the *baraita*] teaches refer to [the wife's statement, as reported by the agent,] "Your wife said: Receive [my bill of divorce for me]," and [the expression] "deliver and give [it] to her" that it teaches refers to "Your wife said: Bring [me my bill of divorce]," and it teaches regarding both of them: once the bill of divorce reaches her hand, she is divorced. And [this is] a refutation of Rav Nachman from [the case of] receipt [responding] to receipt: for [the *baraita*] teaches [a case where she said] "Bring me my bill of divorce," and [the agent said] "Your wife said: Receive [it for me]," and he [the husband] says "Receive [it for her]" — where he explicitly gave it to him in the capacity of receipt, and the husband is not legally empowered for this [to appoint an agent for receipt], and she too did not appoint him [an agent for receipt], yet [the *baraita*] teaches that he is nevertheless an agent for delivery, because since he set his mind to divorce her, etc., as [explained] above; and all the more so where he said to him, "Here it is for you as she said," where one can say he did not rely on [the agent's] words, but rather made it dependent on her intent, and he [the husband] also appointed him an agent for delivery:

Tosafot on Gittin 63a:14:1.hebrew: רבי אומר בכולן אם רצה לחזור לא יחזור - דהולך כזבי, ואע"ג דבסוף פ"ק (לעיל גיטין דף יד:) סבר ר' יהודה הנשיא, דהיינו רבי, דהולך לאו כזכי גבי "הולך מנה לפלוני", שאני הכא, כיון שאמר ליה שליח "אשתך אמרה: קבל לי גיטי", סתמא דמילתא דאדעתא דהכי יהיב ליה:
Tosafot on Gittin 63a:14:1.english: Rabbi says: In all of them, if he seeks to retract, he cannot retract - For "deliver" is like "acquire." And even though at the end of the first chapter (above, Gittin 14b), Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi — who is Rabbi — holds that "deliver" is not like "acquire" regarding [the case of] "Deliver a maneh to so-and-so," here it is different: since the agent said to him, "Your wife said: 'Receive my get for me,'" ordinarily he gives [it] to him with that intention:

Tosafot on Gittin 63a:1:1.hebrew: בשלמא אי איתמר איפכא - בלא איפכא הוי מצי למימר: בשלמא אי אמר רב נחמן "משהגיע גט לידה מגורשת", הוה ש"מ דאדיבורא דידה סמיך; אלא משום דבאיתמר איפכא איכא תרי גווני, נקטיה:
Tosafot on Gittin 63a:1:1.english: Granted, if the opposite was stated - Without "the opposite," [the Gemara] could have said: "Granted, if Rav Naḥman had said, 'Once the bill of divorce reaches her hand, she is divorced,' we would have inferred from this that he relies upon her statement"; rather, because in "if the opposite was stated" there are two ways, it stated it [this way]:
